summary: This resolution expresses the sense of the House that federal, state, and local government employees and uniformed service members should be commended for defending the Constitution and delivering essential services, and calls on the public to observe Public Service Recognition Week with programs and activities honoring their work.

scores.thoughts: The resolution commends public servants and their role in government but contains no provisions, authorizations, or directives related to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget policy. It is purely symbolic recognition.
No references to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures appear in the text.
The bill does not address healthcare systems, coverage, funding, or regulation.
No content related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The resolution makes no mention of immigration policy, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
No discussion of reproductive rights or abortion access.
While uniformed services are mentioned in passing as public servants, the resolution does not address defense spending, military policy, or force structure.
No provisions or statements concerning environmental regulations or climate policy.
The text praises public servants who deliver services but proposes no changes to welfare programs, entitlements, or safety-net funding.
No references to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The resolution does not engage with drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related issues.
No content on sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No discussion of trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill contains no statements on deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions addressing LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The resolution does not mention foreign aid or international assistance.
No content related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
While public servants (many of whom are union members) are praised, the resolution offers no policy changes affecting union rights, collective bargaining, or labor law.
No references to religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination policy.
